title: Embargoed Rollout Readiness Canvas & SLO Calibration Notes
body:
Purpose:
- Create a lightweight, action-oriented canvas that maps the embargoed rollout steps for a major reliability change (SLO tuning + rollout gating) and surface cross-functional responsibilities.
- Focus on measurable verification steps that validate SLOs under production-like traffic before wide release.

Scope:
- Applies to: infra changes, KV-cache behavior tweaks, batching/quantization profiles that affect p95/p99 latency or token-level cost metrics.
- Excludes: model architecture changes and customer-visible API contract changes (those follow release-engineering plan).

Outcome / Success criteria (what "done" looks like):
1) Canary traffic runs for 72 hours with error budget burn <= 15% on targeted SLOs (p95 latency, availability).
2) Telemetry dashboards updated with labeled canary cohort and alerting thresholds validated.
3) Runbook updated with explicit rollback triggers and time-to-restoration targets.
4) Stakeholder signoffs: SRE, Platform, Product (hosted API), and Solutions Eng.

High-level timeline (example 3-week cadence):
- Week 0 (Pre-team prep): create canvas, identify owners, schedule canary window.
- Week 1 (Canary & smoke): 24h smoke then ramp to 5% traffic, run verification tests.
- Week 2 (Extended canary): hold at 5% for 72h with deep telemetry checks, begin downstream partner tests.
- Week 3 (Gradual rollout / ramp): 5% -> 25% -> 100% by policy, with gates at each step.

Key stakeholders & responsibilities (compact):
- SRE lead (Samir Patel): owns canary orchestration, alert gating, emergency rollback.
- Platform eng (Ethan Park): implements config toggles, launch flags, autoscaling policies.
- Product-hosted-api (Ava Liu): customer impact assessment, release comms, acceptance criteria.
- Solutions Eng / CS (Rita Gomez): external partner smoke tests and post-rollout verification.
- Oncall rotation: named responder for canary window; shadow responder from platform team.

Embargo window checklist (pre-rollout):
- [ ] Canary deployment artifact built and hash pinned (PR: #978).
- [ ] Launch flag gated and documented in feature-flags dashboard.
- [ ] Telemetry queries prepared and reviewed: latency_by_route, error_rate_by_customer, kv_cache_hitratio.
- [ ] Synthetic test suite updated with 3 golden prompts and 2 adversarial prompts.
- [ ] Load-job configuration for canary traffic (match seq-length distribution) uploaded.
- [ ] Oncall rota assigned and escalation tree shared to Slack.#sre-ops.
- [ ] Communication embargo start/end time announced to GTM and support.

Verification tests (what to run during canary):
- Smoke: health endpoints, readiness probes, basic inference correctness checks.
- Latency: p50/p95/p99 on target routes compared vs baseline, maintain within +15% p95.
- Availability: 99.9% success on request path for canary cohort.
- Cost delta: token-level cost should not exceed baseline by >20% without approval.
- Quality: automated evals on held-out prompt set; human review for any regression flagged.

SLO calibration experiments (notes):
- Use 7-day rolling baseline but apply a trimmed mean to remove known outliers (deploy spikes).
- Run a controlled burn experiment: intentionally add synthetic latency to validate alert thresholds and escalation cadence.
- Add a derived metric: "canary-error-budget-burn-rate" to normalize across services.

Error budget policy (short):
- If burn > 25% in 24h window -> pause rollout, trigger incident review.
- If burn > 50% cumulative across 72h -> full rollback to previous artifact.
- Rapid remediation: reduce canary traffic and switch to fallback model variant.

Rollback & mitigation triggers (explicit):
- Trigger if p95 latency > baseline + 50% for >30m.
- Trigger if availability < 99% for canary cohort over 15m.
- Trigger if customer-impacting errors appear in top-10 customers list.

Telemetry queries and dashboards (owner: SRE):
- Dashboard: "embargoed-rollout / canary cohort" includes: latency_by_route, error_rate_by_route, token_cost_by_request_type, kv_cache_hitratio, gpu_utilization.
- Alerts: configure high-noise suppression for expected ramp effects; use suppression window tied to rollout stage.

Sprint agenda for cross-functional verification meeting (30–45m):
- 00-05m: Quick status: canary traffic %, health checks.
- 05-15m: Telemetry anomalies and outstanding alerts.
- 15-25m: Quality signals: eval results, human checks.
- 25-35m: Risk review and immediate action items (rollback? throttle?).
- 35-45m: Decisions & assignments; update runbook and comms.

Runbook stub (to be copied into primary runbooks):
- Immediate steps for SRE responder: identify canary cohort, gather logs, attach query links, hit rollback toggle.
- Platform steps: reduce traffic weight by feature-flag -> 0.
- Product steps: notify customers in affected cohort, open support ticket for top customers.

Open questions / unknowns (notes-to-self):
- How to automatically label canary traffic across edge proxies so metrics don't mix? (ticket INF-4332).
- Should we create a short-lived canary KMS key to isolate logs? pros/cons?
- Need agreement on cost delta threshold for experiments that increase per-token cost.

Action items (owner -> next step):
- Samir -> prepare canary dashboard and test alert suppression rules (due 2026-01-18).
- Ethan -> add launch flag and safe rollback toggle to runtime config (PR #978).
- Rita -> schedule partner validation window and collect sample queries (due 2026-01-20).
- Maya -> finalize canvas and circulate to stakeholders, create confluence summary.

Notes / informal: 
- This canvas intentionally conservative: prefer to slow ramp vs noisy rollback.
- Keep human-in-loop for first two ramps; we can automate subsequent ramps after three successful canaries.
- If we detect model quality drift separate from infra noise, escalate to Applied ML with full eval set.

References & quick links:
- Confluence: Embargoed Rollouts playbook (see linked_artifacts).
- Jira: INF-4321 (canary tagging), INF-4332 (telemetry labeling).
- PR: serving-runtime #978 (feature flag and rollout toggle).
